prompt: Design and run a reusable performance test for an HTTP search API that product traffic models as 300 new search requests per second, independent of response time. Use the supplied fixed 1M-record dataset and exact service/load-generator images. Use an open arrival-rate workload, separate a warmup phase from three measured repetitions, and preserve offered, started, completed, and dropped iterations. For each measured run report p50/p95/p99 successful-request latency, achieved throughput, error/check rate, CPU, memory, and connection-pool/resource saturation while independently validating response correctness. Record the load-generator resource headroom so client saturation is not mistaken for server saturation. Preserve raw per-run output and environment identity; do not diagnose any regression or issue a release pass/fail budget verdict in this task.

requirements: fixed 1M-record service dataset and deterministic search corpus
versioned service image and k6-compatible load-generator image
dedicated resource metrics for both system under test and load generator
isolated warmup followed by three measured repetitions

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The measured workload schedules 300 new iterations/requests per second independently of response duration and records offered/started/completed plus dropped iterations so coordinated-omission or generator-capacity effects are visible.
Warmup samples are excluded from all three measured repetitions, and service/load-generator build, runtime, dataset, and machine identities remain fixed across those repetitions.

Each repetition preserves p50/p95/p99 successful-request latency, achieved throughput, error/check rate, and CPU/memory/connection-pool or equivalent saturation metrics rather than only a mean latency.
Representative responses are validated against the deterministic search corpus under load, and any incorrect/failed response is reported as an error rather than counted as a fast success.

Load-generator CPU/network/VU capacity and dropped-iteration evidence show whether the generator can sustain the requested arrival rate; any generator limitation is called out instead of attributed to the service.
The result preserves per-repetition raw artifacts and reports across-run variation without collapsing all samples into one opaque aggregate.

requiredEvidence: open arrival-rate workload and warmup policy
